text: WEMo (Wave Exposure Model) R package implements simplified hydrodynamic model quantify wind-wave exposure coastal inland waters. uses linear wave theory estimate wave height energy, accounting local water depth effects like shoaling wave breaking. combines wind data, shoreline geometry, bathymetry estimate wave conditions reproducible scriptable workflow R. package provides modern, open-source, accessible implementation original WEMo, developed NOAA’s Center Coastal Fisheries Habitat Research previously required proprietary plug-ESRI’s ArcMap software. original tool longer compatible modern GIS software, R package provides sustainable license-free path forward researchers resource managers. addition core modeling functionality, package provides dynamic tools gathering preparing input data visualizing results. info original WEMo : https://coastalscience.noaa.gov/science-areas/climate-change/wemo/

title: Calculate Effective Fetch for Wind Energy Transfer — effective_fetch
text: Effective fetch WEMo calculated summing product fetch length cosine angle departure ith heading n number fetch rays dividing sum cosine angles. Effective fetch rays look trimmed figure compared fetch rays. method based assumption wind moving water surface transfers energy water direction wind directions within 4/pi radians (45) either side wind direction. (USCOE 1977) function processes site independently calculates effective fetch using cosine-weighted average fetch rays within specified angular cone around target direction. calculation follows: $$Eff F_{} = \frac{\sum_{j=-n}^{n} F_j \cos(\theta_j)}{\sum_{j= -n}^{n} \cos(\theta_j)}$$ : $$Eff F_i$$ Effective fetch ith direction fetch ray $$F_j$$ length j radiating fetch ray clipping shoreline $$\theta_j$$ angle ith fetch ray jth ray $$n$$ number rays selected user function handles directional wrap-around expanding direction space ±360 ensure proper calculation near 0/360 boundary.
